conflict: the protagonist returns to the wrecked inspection train and its working brake-light/horn system and converts wreckage into a rescue/trap system using freight conductor knowledge
power_position_end: occupational author of the rescue mechanism
turn: the protagonist returns to the wrecked inspection train and its working brake-light/horn system and converts wreckage into a rescue/trap system using freight conductor knowledge
protagonist_decision: risk noise, light, fire, or machinery that can attract the predator in order to control where it goes
subtext: Professional identity becomes agency when it converts wreckage into a plan.

visual_action.first_image: Ilsa crawls through the wrecked inspection train and its working brake-light/horn system, opens panels, pulls wires, braces doors, and tests improvised light or sound barriers
visual_action.face_reaction: the protagonist's expression shifts from guilt toward controlled attention when the turn lands
visual_action.vertical_composition: vulnerable or morally important figures remain visually legible while status power occupies height, threshold, or audience control
visual_action.final_image: cracked red brake-light lens locks into the mechanism and the first controlled test flashes/sounds through the wreck

dialogue_design.function: make choices, objections, and proof implications audible rather than explaining theme
dialogue_design.subtext_rule: characters negotiate status, debt, permission, blame, and care; they rarely name the theme directly
key_lines: The light can hold it. Help me keep the line open.

opposition_beats.dramatic_job: preparing the wrecked inspection train and its working brake-light/horn system requires noise, light, heat, or movement that can attract a tunnel-sized centipede with a black glass shell
opposition_beats.writing_note: pressure is spatial, sensory, mechanical, or creature behavior rather than villain exposition

opposition_beats.voice: a dust-blue giant moth whose wings react to light
opposition_beats.dramatic_job: a failed test may waste the only working mechanism
opposition_beats.writing_note: the objection is embodied by vulnerability, hesitation, warning, or creature behavior

opposition_beats.dramatic_job: Ilsa uses freight conductor knowledge to convert wreckage into a controlled trap/rescue system
opposition_beats.writing_note: the decision must be visible through action before any sparse dialogue validates it

opposition_beats.dramatic_job: cracked red brake-light lens becomes the key operating part of the final mechanism
opposition_beats.writing_note: end with changed access, proof, injury, creature response, or a plan component rather than explanation

spoken_exchange.speaker: Ilsa
spoken_exchange.line: The light can hold it. Help me keep the line open.
spoken_exchange.action: Ilsa braces the mechanism while pointing to the open path
spoken_exchange.subtext: competence becomes shared action without surrendering authorship
spoken_exchange.power_move: practical survival pressure answered through protection, restraint, rescue, or recognition
spoken_exchange.listening_response: the next action answers the immediate bodily danger rather than explaining theme
spoken_exchange.status_shift: the speaker converts fear or doubt into a concrete survival obligation
spoken_exchange.room_sound: breath, debris, creature texture, machinery, weather, and animal vocalization remain present beneath the sparse line

dialogue_design.scene_rhythm: visual objective first; sparse dialogue only validates choices after action, creature behavior, or mechanical proof has already made them legible
rewrite_directives: write objectives that remain understandable with sound off
use creature behavior, terrain, tools, animal reaction, and occupational action instead of exposition
allow breath, silence, machinery, and small animal sound to carry emotion before score
keep any spoken line short, practical, and subordinate to the visual decision

sound_design.dialogue_priority: dialogue is sparse and practical; breath, creature texture, machinery, weather, footsteps, and animal vocalization carry most narrative information
sound_design.music_function: mechanical clicks, electrical charge, tool rhythm, metal stress, cloth movement, and brief failed-test silence
sound_design.silence_or_negative_space: sound rhythm turns preparation into suspense rather than montage noise
sound_design.motif: cracked red brake-light lens clicks/scrapes, predator texture, small animal vocalization, and mechanical air/light rhythm

edit_hook.entry_hook: enter on the immediate consequence of the previous turn: a trapped railway pigeon with a red leg band or a survivor contributes one small behavior that completes the plan without stealing protagonist agency
edit_hook.exit_hook: will the improvised machine work once, or attract the predator too early?

failure_checks: Does the scene change power, trust, evidence, capability, or relational obligation?
Is the object/space doing narrative work rather than decorative worldbuilding?
Is public or institutional pressure expressed through visible behavior rather than exposition?
Does the protagonist retain agency instead of being rescued into passivity?
